content.title: About
content.content: Grape leaves stuffed with rice is a classic dish of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisine. Tender grape leaves are filled with a seasoned rice mixture, often enriched with herbs, spices, and sometimes minced meat, then simmered or baked until tender.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grape leaves have been used in cooking for over 2,000 years, mentioned in ancient Roman culinary texts.
The dish is popular in Greece (dolmadakia), Turkey (dolma), and the Balkans, each region adding its own spice blend.
Grape leaves are rich in antioxidants, particularly polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.
Traditionally the rolls are served with a lemon‑olive oil drizzle or a yogurt‑based sauce for brightness.
Leaves can be preserved in brine, allowing year‑round use.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Both rice and grape leaves provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The dish is typically prepared with minimal added oil, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice supplies thiamine (B1) and pyridoxine (B6), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytochemicals in grape leaves help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium in the leaves aids in blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Grape allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to grape leaves.

items.title: Sodium content in brine
items.content: Preserved leaves are often stored in salty brine; people with hypertension should rinse them well before use.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of fiber can cause discomfort for those with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rolls warm or at room temperature, drizzled with lemon juice, yogurt sauce, or tomato sauce. They can be enjoyed as a snack, part of a mezze platter, or as a main course. Some variations include adding ground beef or lamb to the rice filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep canned grape leaves in the refrigerator, sealed in their brine, and use within 3‑5 days after opening. Fresh leaves should be wrapped in a damp cloth and stored in the fridge, best used within 2 days.
